corrections.q: 43. Shaw cited Charles Lever's novel entitled:
corrections.reason: Shaw names Charles Lever’s novel A Day’s Ride: A Life’s Romance; “A Day’s Romance” is not the title, so “All of the above” cannot be correct.

corrections.q: 86. After graduating from Trinity College in Dublin in 1928, Samuel Beckett travelled to Paris to teach English.
corrections.reason: Beckett graduated from Trinity in 1927 and went to Paris in 1928; the statement incorrectly makes the graduation year 1928.

corrections.q: 102. Major Barbara took place over the course of three days.
corrections.reason: Act I occurs on a January night, Act II the next morning, and Act III on the following day after lunch: three calendar days.

corrections.q: 118. The Fabian society which Shaw joined adopted a dogmatic approach to reforming English.
corrections.reason: Fabian reform is gradual, practical, empirical, and pluralist rather than dogmatic.

corrections.q: 120. Shaw wrote Progress and Poverty in 1882.
corrections.reason: Progress and Poverty was written by Henry George and published in 1879; Shaw encountered George’s ideas, but did not author the book.

corrections.q: 121. Widowers' Houses was banned from the theatre for sexual profanity.
corrections.reason: Widowers’ Houses was produced in 1892. Mrs Warren’s Profession—not Widowers’ Houses—was the Shaw play banned/censored over its sexual subject matter.

corrections.q: 154. Shaw's Preface to Major Barbara consists of:
corrections.reason: The Project Gutenberg preface text has seven titled divisions, not six.

corrections.q: 162. When Barbara became disappointed with the Salvation Army, Bill Walker:
corrections.reason: Bill Walker taunts/sneers at Barbara after the Salvation Army accepts the money; “gloated” matches the scene, whereas “pitied her” does not.

corrections.q: 36. The narrative time a certain event takes in the story is called "story time".
corrections.reason: Story time is the duration/order of events in the story world; the item’s own feedback already states this and contradicts its stored key.

corrections.q: The epic poem ends with Odysseus and Penelope being reunited and living happily ever after.
corrections.reason: The poem ends after the reunion and restoration of peace, but Tiresias has already foretold further travel; “living happily ever after” overstates the ending.
